shorts.title: What you will learn: Lambda functions
shorts.hook: A function that fits on one line.
shorts.script: A function that fits on one line. Today we write functions without names. Lambdas are small, quick and common in modern C plus plus. A lambda is a small function without a name. It has square brackets, then parameters, then a body. The square brackets say which outside variables the lambda may use. You can store a lambda in an auto variable and call it like a function. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: Offset is one hundred. The capture list names offset. The lambda keeps a copy of it. The body adds the offset to x. Shift of five gives one hundred and five. The program prints one hundred and five. A lambda is a small function without a name. Square brackets capture outside variables. Store a lambda in an auto variable. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A variable that is not captured
shorts.script: Bug of the Day. The lambda uses offset, but the capture list is empty. The compiler says offset is not captured. A lambda cannot see outside variables unless you list them. Write offset between the square brackets. A lambda can only use outside variables that you list in its square brackets. Add offset to the capture list. A lambda is a small function without a name. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
